EMU128_X86_64 SumWideningSpanU32 the port has fewer instructions but more branches (6 against 4, 11 against 8 and 8 against 6): LLVM unrolls the port's much smaller kernel loop (two 16-byte iterations per pass for LargestDigit, four 4-byte iterations per pass for SumWidening) behind a prologue that peels the odd iterations (testb $0x10 or $0xc, jne or je)
EMU128_X86_64 TableLookupBytesI8 the port looks up the 16 bytes without branches (andl of the index, a movzbl load from a stack copy of the table, movd), merges them with SIMD unpacks (punpcklbw, punpcklwd, punpckldq, punpcklqdq) and zeroes the out-of-range lanes with one pminub, pcmpeqb and pand (103 instructions); highway's EMU128 tests each index with cmpb and ja around a movzbl and a shift (shll, shlq) and merges the bytes in general-purpose registers (166 instructions)
